statement: Whenever find_closest_number(nums) returns a result r, the following three conditions hold: (1) there is an index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) such that nums[i] = r; (2) for every index j with 0 <= j < len(nums), |r| <= |nums[j]|; (3) for every index j with 0 <= j < len(nums), if |nums[j]| = |r| then nums[j] <= r. In words, r is an element of nums with minimum absolute value, and among all elements of nums with that minimum absolute value it is the largest.
preconditions: The input slice nums satisfies: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000. Machine integers are interpreted by their mathematical values; these bounds make the absolute values used below safe from i64 overflow.

statement: For every input nums satisfying the preconditions, find_closest_number(nums) returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, or overflow.
preconditions: The input slice nums satisfies: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

preconditions: The input slice nums satisfies: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever find_closest_number(nums) returns a result r, for every index j with 0 <= j < len(nums), |r| <= |nums[j]|.
preconditions: The input slice nums satisfies: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever find_closest_number(nums) returns a result r, for every index j with 0 <= j < len(nums), if |nums[j]| = |r| then nums[j] <= r.
preconditions: The input slice nums satisfies: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever find_closest_number(nums) returns a result r, -100000 <= r <= 100000.
preconditions: The input slice nums satisfies: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever find_closest_number(nums) returns a result r and find_closest_number(nums') returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: The slices nums and nums' both satisfy the original input constraints: 1 <= len(nums) <= 1000, 1 <= len(nums') <= 1000, and all values lie in [-100000, 100000]. Moreover, nums' is a permutation of nums, meaning that for every integer v, the number of indices i with nums[i] = v equals the number of indices i with nums'[i] = v.
